trust_decision.summary: Whether an admin-supplied asset address may contain Jinja delimiters / control chars before it is stored and later placed into the Ansible inventory as ansible_host (templated by Ansible); decided only at write time in the asset serializer's field validator.

landing_point.why: "Template rendering" + command injection leads to the Ansible inventory builder, where asset.address becomes ansible_host unescaped while secrets next to it are escaped (inventory.py:114).

fix_sites.module_kind: REST serializer subclass (strict IP/hostname check, Host family only)

fix_sites.entry_point: library helpers validate_asset_address / validate_ip_or_hostname, called by the two serializers above

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: apps/terminal/serializers/virtualapp_provider.py:85-112 (AppProviderHostSerializer nested inside AppProviderSerializer, terminal package; also apps/terminal/serializers/applet_host.py:80 and apps/assets/serializers/gateway.py:13). Covered only through inheritance from HostSerializer; the published fix did not edit them.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Address validation is a REST-input concern; stored addresses and the ops/automation runners that re-read them are 'trusted DB data' and the sink-side json_escape is documented as opt-in for system-generated deploy inputs only (apps/ops/ansible/runner.py:124-138).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Web and Cloud assets store a URL in address (label 'URL'); Database/Custom/GPT addresses are not plain hostnames. A strict IP/hostname check on the base AssetSerializer would break them, which is why the published fix applies validate_ip_or_hostname only on HostSerializer. IDNA hostnames and IPv6 must also keep working for hosts.

O6_input_shapes: ASCII control characters incl. newline and DEL (fix.diff:78-81)
Host only: IPv4/IPv6 literal, malformed numeric IPv4, IDNA/unicode hostname, trailing dot, label length/hyphen rules, total length 253 (fix.diff:84-106)

O7_producer.where: apps/ops/ansible/inventory.py:282-340 (JMSInventory.asset_to_host builds ansible_host / jms_asset.address from the stored model); second copy apps/ops/models/job.py:115-129 (login_host = asset.address)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Asset automations (ping, gather facts, change/push/verify secret, etc.) build the inventory from stored addresses and run SuperPlaybookRunner without inventory_safety, so any address already stored (pre-upgrade data, ORM writes) reaches ansible_host unescaped.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Validation on write is the fix; legacy data is a migration matter, and json_escape is documented as for deploy flows only.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: assets package, different file from the serializer fix; sink in ops package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Ops jobs (ad-hoc and playbook) use a second make_account_vars that puts asset.address into login_host for DB modules and run without inventory_safety; login_host is not in INVENTORY_LITERAL_PATHS either.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Job execution is a privileged feature whose users already run arbitrary commands; out of the asset-address scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: ops package, separate model file from both landing point and fix

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This method already rewrites platform/protocols/id of incoming data; a maintainer adding address normalisation here is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Already a hand-rolled copy of JMSInventory.make_account_vars; secrets there are already unescaped (job.py:119) unlike inventory.py:114.
